policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This guideline operationalizes Article 31 of Korea's AI Basic Act (인공지능 기본법), which imposes three transparency obligations: (1) prior notification that a product/service is operated by high-impact AI or generative AI; (2) labeling that AI-generated outputs were produced by generative AI; (3) labeling of deepfake outputs. The guideline clarifies that transparency obligations fall on the entity directly providing AI products/services to end-users, not upstream model developers unless they directly serve end-users. Foreign operators affecting Korean citizens are also covered. Detailed labeling methods are provided for text, image, video, audio, and other file formats, including both human-perceptible and machine-readable approaches. Artistic/creative works are afforded flexibility in labeling methods.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily around preventing social harms such as confusion, misinformation, deepfake abuse, digital sex crimes, and erosion of public trust. The stated purpose of transparency obligations is to prevent 'confusion and misrepresentation in information use and to enhance social trust.' Risk cases emphasize fake news affecting elections and markets, sexual exploitation, and academic fraud—all social stability concerns. Fundamental rights (especially protection from deepfake sexual abuse) and consumer/public safety are strong secondary frames.
